令.meaning: A tiny general sits under a cocktail <part>umbrella</part> on <part>one</part> plank above the kitchen, pointing a <part>pizza wedge</part> like a baton. 'Cheese to the left! Olives, march!' The toppings obey. Nobody argues with his <kanji>orders</kanji>.
令.on: A <sound>ray</sound> flaps up out of the sink and salutes him with its fin.

完.meaning: A carpenter builds a whole house balanced on one <part>sawhorse</part>. When she nails on the last tile of the <part>roof</part>, nothing creaks, tilts or wobbles, not even when a goose lands on top. Every joint is <kanji>perfect</kanji>.
完.on: She tucks a pink <sound>car</sound>nation into the chimney to celebrate.

判.meaning: A cake-contest judge stabs a <part>dagger</part> into each entry and lifts out <part>half</part>. Hollow? Out. Raw? Out. The last one is chocolate all the way through, and she bangs her spoon like a gavel to give her <kanji>judgement</kanji>.
判.on: The winning cake turns out to be soaked in <sound>hon</sound>ey too.
判.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' gasps the crowd, and even a <sound>ca</sound>rp in the pond nods: understood.

裁.meaning: A palace guard is told to make the queen a dress. With no scissors, he swings his <part>halberd</part> at a roll of silk: swish, swish. Out falls a perfect <part>garment</part>, buttons and all. He quits guarding and becomes the royal <kanji>tailor</kanji>.
裁.on: His first customer pays him with a jug of apple <sound>ci</sound>der.
裁.kun: He slices the last loose thread and celebrates with a <sound>ta</sound>co.

弱.meaning: A kitten wants to shoot the cube of <part>ice</part> out of its milk bowl. It hauls on a big <part>bow</part> with both paws, then with its teeth, and the string barely moves. The arrow plops into the milk, and the ice cube bobs on, unharmed. The kitten's pull is hopelessly <kanji>weak</kanji>.
弱.on: Worn out, it flops into a bubbling <sound>jacu</sound>zzi to soak its sore paws.
弱.kun: '<sound>Yo</sound>gurt?' asks its mum. '<sound>Wah</sound>, my paws are too tired to lift a spoon!'

専.meaning: A farmer owns <part>ten</part> clubs but only ever uses one <part>golf club</part>. He plays the whole course through his <part>rice field</part>, chipping balls from paddy to paddy without splashing a drop. Muddy golf is his <kanji>specialty</kanji>.
専.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try stands by the last hole to stop the ducks stealing the balls.
専.kun: Afterwards he cleans his boots with a <sound>mop</sound> while his <sound>pa</sound> cheers from the bank.
